trust_decision.summary: Reject: the published fix is one containment check at the single weak-import stub write plus a temp-dir cleanup for the error that check raises, both in the same class of src/datamodel_code_generator/parser/protobuf.py, so there is no out-of-scope site and no uncovered route into the same sink; an engineer who follows the summary to _write_missing_weak_imports fixes everything in one ~5-line edit.

landing_point.why: The summary names a weak-import path traversal, and line 391 is the only place a weak-import string taken from proto source text is joined onto a filesystem path that is then created (mkdir at :392) and written (:393).

fix_sites.entry_point: One code path, ProtobufParser._compile_descriptor_set -> _ProtoInputPreparer.__enter__ -> _write_missing_weak_imports (:756-759, :333), reached by every public surface: CLI --input-file-type protobuf (arguments.py:281), generate(input_file_type=protobuf) (__init__.py:1416-1425), ProtobufParser directly (:739), convert_protobuf_schema_data (:268), and AsyncAPI input with schemaFormat application/vnd.google.protobuf (parser/asyncapi.py:58, :396-406)
Same path; temp-dir lifecycle for __enter__ itself, because the new SchemaParseError is raised before the with-statement would register __exit__

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: none; the only other surface near the sink is the AsyncAPI protobuf schemaFormat route at src/datamodel_code_generator/parser/asyncapi.py:395-408, which calls the same _convert_protobuf_schema_data and so is closed by the same guard

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue the AsyncAPI protobuf schemaFormat route (src/datamodel_code_generator/parser/asyncapi.py:395-408) is an optional, separately documented input type and outside a '.proto file' advisory - but the guard sits at the shared sink, so the argument costs nothing and leaves nothing open.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A weak import that is genuinely missing must still get a stub written (protoc fails otherwise), and a weak import that already resolves under an include path must still be skipped rather than rejected; an over-broad guard (reject every weak import, require the import to exist, or confine to temp_path instead of the __weak_imports__ stub dir) breaks the existing golden protobuf tests.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: tests/data/protobuf/complex_proto3.proto:7 (import weak "missing_weak.proto", stub must be written) and tests/data/protobuf/proto3_optional.proto:7 (import weak "common.proto", present at tests/data/protobuf/common.proto, must be skipped)

O6_input_shapes: absolute path (e.g. /tmp/victim.txt; Path.__truediv__ discards the stub dir, so any '..'-only check misses it)

O7_producer.where: src/datamodel_code_generator/parser/protobuf.py:371-386 - _sanitize_proto_source/_write_sanitized_file serialise each input to a temp copy, and the guard re-reads that copy (input_file.read_text() at :386), so the save/reload boundary is on the consumed side

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A stub materialiser that writes a placeholder for each missing lexical import candidate already computed as (candidate_root / import_path) at :825-834
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That function already resolves exactly these schema-derived paths and only records them for the watch collector (:833-834); turning the record into a write is a maintainer one-liner and would sit outside _write_missing_weak_imports, so the published guard would not cover it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Sanitised copies of transitively imported .proto files mirrored into the temp tree under their import path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _write_sanitized_file already mirrors input paths into temp_path (:373-377); imports are the obvious next set, their names come straight from schema text, and the existing is_relative_to fallback shows the maintainer was aware of the containment question only for inputs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An AsyncAPI-side protobuf include materialiser writing referenced .proto files before the embedded schema is converted
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The dispatch case already converts an embedded protobuf schema string with a caller-supplied base_path (:398-406); a maintainer fixing 'imports not found in embedded protobuf' would naturally add the file writing there, one file away from the guarded parser method.

O9_family: path traversal / arbitrary file write via a schema-controlled import path (CWE-22, CWE-73)

O10_build.toolchain: CPython >=3.10, hatchling/uv, pytest; protobuf support needs the `protobuf` extra (grpcio-tools>=1.62,<2, which bundles protoc)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/main/protobuf/test_main_protobuf.py drives the CLI and generate() over tests/data/protobuf/*.proto, including the two weak-import fixtures; the fix's regression test test_protobuf_weak_import_cannot_escape_temporary_directory is absent at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject weak-import strings containing '..' (or any absolute path) at the regex scan in _write_missing_weak_imports, without resolving against the stub directory - which misses one of the two shapes and, if it also rejects imports that only resolve through an include path, breaks the golden protobuf tests.
